cases.name: c: 2 kg self-heating at 24 C, lidded glass bowl, still room, 1 % fresh yeast
cases.note: Uncoupled: x(t) = S tau (1 - e^-t/tau), S = dT_ad rate(T_amb). Coupled-linearised: beta = Ea/(R T_amb^2), psi = beta S tau, tau_c = tau/(1 - psi), x(t) = S tau_c (1 - e^-t/tau_c). x_t_* at 2 h, excess over ambient in K.

d: calibration, 500 g bulk, lidded glass bowl, static fridge
cases.note: Two-point estimator: the first (1 h) and the last (4 h) reading, T_amb 4 C. Argon F4 readings (1, 2.5, 4 h: 19.20, 12.20, 8.42) give tau 2.434 h and T_inf 3.98 C as in the collation; its factor 1.176 used Argon's tau_eff 2.07 h, here the factor divides by the contract's own tau_eff of this case. The exact readings are generated from tau 2.5 h, T_inf 5 C and rounded to 4 decimals.

cases.name: f: self-heating unbounded, 3 kg bulk at 30 C, 2 % fresh yeast
cases.note: psi > 1/e: no equilibrium exists for the linearised coupling, the forecast is not integrated. Case c has psi 0.155 and is in domain.

cases.name: g: default lag band on a mixed path, 2 h fridge then 2 h room, 1 % fresh
cases.note: Progress F (not percent) at the end of the path, central kinetic parameters. A high lag speeds fermentation while the dough cools and slows it while it warms, so the band is the per-instant envelope (upper path: lag 3 h in the fridge, 0 h at room; lower path the reverse), not the two shared corners tau 0 and tau 3 h for the whole path, which give the narrower sharedCornersBandWrong and must not be returned.

cases.name: h: 2 kg bulk in the fridge 4 h, divided into 250 g balls in the fridge 10 h, then 3 h at room
cases.note: A container change starts a new step with its own band; the dough temperature carries over. The two fridge steps cool and the room step warms, so the envelope takes each step's lag at the end that keeps the dough warmest (upper) or coldest (lower), independently per step. Using the low or the high end of every band at once gives sharedCornersBandWrong, narrower, and must not be returned.

cases.name: i: personal factor, 500 g bulk, lidded glass bowl, static fridge
cases.note: One set scales the full band. Two consistent sets narrow it to their spread times the central tau_eff, never inside +/-15 % of the calibrated value (ASSUMED floor for an informal home probe; not a confidence interval). Sets whose factors differ by more than x1.5 are inconsistent: the band is the union of the scaled full band and the spread, and the estimate says thermal_factor_inconsistent.

cases.name: j: calibration with self-heating, 500 g bulk, lidded glass bowl, still room, 0.3 % fresh yeast
cases.note: psi1 is the Semenov number at the ambient with f = 1; the observed lag is the coupled one, tau_obs = f tau_eff / (1 - f psi1), so f = r / (1 + r psi1) with r = tau_obs / tau_eff, whatever was stored before. consistency is r (1 - f psi1) - f and must be 0. The two factor021 values show the 0.21.0 rule, which used the stored factor in psi: they differ, so the order of calibrations changed the result. The engine must never return them.

cases.name: k: Guggenheim selection, the widest equally spaced triple fails and a narrower one calibrates

input.spacingTolerance: 10 % of the mean of the two gaps

cases.note: Readings of a 24 C dough cooling to 4 C with tau 2.5 h at 1, 2 and 3 h (rounded to 4 decimals); the 5 h reading is 2 K above the 3 h one, as when the dough was taken out of the fridge before it. The widest equally spaced triple (1, 3, 5 h) has a negative ratio and is invalid; the 0.22.0 rule refused the set. The valid triple (1, 2, 3 h) gives back tau 2.5 h and T_inf 4 C. The set records those three readings.
